1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version
16	Prelude depends on) rather than from memory. Run `koda-review` before calling a
17	change finished.
18	
19	Koda is the npm package `@kodalang/core`, pinned in `package.json`, and it ships
20	its skills. The ones in `.claude/skills/` are copies of the installed package's;
21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run
22	`npm run skills` to copy them again, and read what changed.
23	
24	## Working here
25	
26	- `npm start` runs Prelude on http://localhost:4200 (`PORT` to change it).
27	  Views are cached when the server starts: restart it after changing one.
28	- `npm test` runs the tests (node --test). Add tests for what you build.

2

I'd keep the title and a one-line branch summary ("check passes · 2 behind main"). The branch details and actions (Update, Merge / Push) would open in a drawer.
2. **The design bar is crowded.** It has about a dozen controls in one row. I'd split them into what you're looking at (page, state, Design/App), what you can do to the page (Send event, Reset data) and approval, which would become a review strip (see 3). Refresh, Open in browser and Pop out would move into one small menu.
3. **Check results lead nowhere.** "2 pages differ" and "1 page doesn't render" only name the pages. Each one could be a link that shows that page in that state in the preview, and the review strip could show the count with Approve beside it.
4. **Pages with `:params` can't be picked.** You can't choose a detail page, or a drawer over one, from the menu; you have to click through in the preview. The page menu could list them with a sample record from the current state.
5. **The design's rules and notes are hidden.** The rules (RULES.md) and the notes' decisions and open questions don't appear anywhere on this page. A side panel could show the rules for the page on show, and the open questions waiting for you.
6. **The status line says little.** "Working…" could show what the agent is doing now (its latest tool step) and how long it has been going.
7. **A new session starts blank.** It could suggest starting points: the open questions from the notes, and pages that don't render.

**How I'd build it:** copy the app's views into this design and mark them `"from": "@app/server/views/…"`, so the build ports the changes back. I'd start with a faithful copy of today's page as the baseline, then make the changes you pick. The states would be:

- a failing check
- pages that differ from their approved versions
- a new design with no sessions
- a build session
- an update from main that clashes
- the preview popped out into its own window

The message box now takes images. You can attach one with the paperclip, paste it into the box, or drop it on the box. I haven't seen it render; Prelude's check after this turn will show whether it does.

**How it works**
- **Thumbnails before sending:** each image uploads as soon as it's added and appears as a thumbnail above the box, with its name and a Remove button. You see exactly what the agent will get before you send.
- **In the conversation:** sent images sit above the message. Each opens full size when clicked.
- **What the agent sees:** the app keeps the images with the session and tells the agent where they are, so it can read them. They're still there when the session is reopened.
- **Images only:** PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP. A message may be images alone, with no words.
- **The box grows as you type,** up to a third of the window, then scrolls.

To see it, the "Typical" state has a napkin sketch and a Figma frame waiting to be sent. The "Popped out" state has a sent screenshot with a problem circled.

**Design system:** thumbnails, the attach button and the drop highlight are now part of the composer component, its gallery and its notes. Other designs can use them.

**Limits of the preview.** These are limits of the preview's fake server only; the real app behaves properly:
- Uploading a real file doesn't produce a thumbnail.
- Thumbnails stay in the box after you send.
- An images-only message is refused, because the fake server can't express "words or an image".

**What else I'd add to the message box,** most useful first:
1. **What you're looking at goes with the message.** A chip such as "Compare offers · Typical · Phone" tells the agent which page, state and size you mean when you say "this". You could remove it when it doesn't apply.
2. **Point at things by name.** Typing @ would offer the design's pages, states, rules and files. "Make @Offer match @napkin-compare.jpg" is then exact.
3. **Send while the agent is working.** Today the agent's working state blocks sending. Instead, your message could wait in line and go when the turn ends, with a way to edit or cancel it.
4. **Drafts kept.** Text and images stay in the box if you switch sessions or reload.
5. **Mark up an image.** Circle or arrow on a screenshot before sending, the way people already do outside Prelude.
6. **Capture the preview.** One click attaches a screenshot of the page on show, at its current size. This needs the server to render it, because the preview is on another origin.
7. **Smaller touches:** up-arrow to edit your last message, and dictation for describing a sketch aloud.

Which would you like next? I'd start with 1 and 3: they remove the most back-and-forth with the agent.

All three are built: clicking a thumbnail opens the image, the message box says what you're looking at, and you can send while the agent works. I haven't seen any of it render; Prelude's check after this turn will show whether it does.

**Clicking a thumbnail** opens the image as large as the window allows, in a dialog with its name and when it was sent. Open in browser shows it at its own size so you can zoom in. It works both for images waiting to be sent and for sent ones. To fit images, the app shell now has a wider version of its dialog, which other designs can use too.

**What you're looking at goes with the message.** A small chip at the foot of the message box reads, for example, "Compare offers · Typical · Phone".
- It follows the page and state as you pick them.
- It adds the size and client of the preview beside the chat, but only when they aren't the defaults (Fit and Browser).
- It's on by default; click it off for a message about something else.
- Each sent message shows what it was about under its bubble.

The chip is now in the design system too, as a general on/off pill.

**Sending while the agent works**
- The box stays open, and Send becomes "Send when it’s done", with a line saying so.
- Each waiting message shows under the conversation, dashed, with Cancel.
- When the agent finishes, they all go to it together, in order, as the next message.
- If you press Stop, nothing waiting is sent: the messages go back into the box for you to send or change. I chose that because stopping usually means you want to redirect the agent; tell me if you'd rather they were sent.

**To see it in the preview**
- "Typical" has the chip, images waiting to be sent, and sent messages with what they were about.
- "Building" has one message waiting.
- "Popped out" has two waiting messages, and a sent screenshot you can click to see full size.

**Limit of the preview:** an image you upload there for real has no full-size view, because the fake server doesn't record it as one of the session's images. The real app behaves properly.

**One question:** should a waiting message be editable, or is Cancel enough? Cancel and retype is enough for now, I think.

The decisions are in `NOTES.md` and three new proposed rules in `RULES.md`. I also changed the design system and app shell, and recorded those changes in their own `NOTES.md` files.

Yes, the desktop app does differ, and mostly for the worse with the design as it stands. But I'd fix that by not relying on either the browser or Windows for dictation.

**Where things stand.** The design uses the browser's built-in speech recognition. Chrome and Edge have it, and send your audio to Google or Microsoft to transcribe. The desktop app's window is Microsoft's WebView2, and as far as I know it doesn't provide that recognition (I haven't confirmed it). So in the desktop app the button would fall back to telling you to press Windows key + H.

**What Windows offers:**
- **Voice typing (Windows key + H)** already works in any text box, the desktop app included, with no work from us. But it's separate from Prelude: Prelude can't start it, or show that it's listening, from its own microphone button.
- **Windows' speech recognition API**, which the desktop app could call itself. The microphone button would then work there and look the same. I'd expect its quality to be about the same as the browser's, so it would only fill the gap in the desktop app.

**What I'd suggest instead: transcribe on your own machine.** Prelude already runs a local server in both clients.
1. The button records audio. Both browsers and WebView2 can do that.
2. The audio goes to Prelude's own server.
3. The server turns it into text with a speech-to-text model on your machine (Whisper).

That would be better in several ways:
- **The same in both clients:** no desktop-only path, and no fallback message.
- **Private:** nothing leaves your machine, so the warning about Google and Microsoft goes away. You'd only grant microphone access.
- **Better with design vocabulary:** Prelude can tell the model the design's own words first: page names, states, "Koda", "ko-target". General-purpose services tend to garble those.

The cost:
- The model is a one-time download, from about 150 MB to over a gigabyte depending on quality.
- Words appear a moment after you stop speaking, not as you talk. That's fine for messages, I think.
- Transcription runs on your machine's processor or graphics card.

Dictation now turns your speech into text on your own machine, the same way in the browser and the desktop app. I haven't seen it render; Prelude's check after this turn will show whether it does. Press Reset data first, as the states changed again.

**Setting it up (once)**
- The first press of the microphone opens a dialog to choose a speech model:
  - **Quick**, 142 MB, English only.
  - **Balanced**, 466 MB, many languages (the default).
  - **Most accurate**, 1.6 GB, best with technical words.
- It says plainly that the model downloads from Hugging Face. That download is the only thing that ever leaves your machine; what you say never does.
- While it downloads, the microphone shows how far it's got, with Cancel. Then it's ready.

**Using it**
1. Press the microphone and speak. The button pulses and the box says "Listening…".
2. Press again. The box says "Typing what you said…", and your words appear after what's already there.
3. Anything you typed while it listened is kept, and the result is saved as a draft like any typing.

The words come after you stop speaking, not as you talk.

Prelude's server runs the model, and gives it the design's own words first (page names, states, components) so it spells them right.

**To see it in the preview**
- "Pages differ": the set-up dialog, when you press the microphone.
- "Building": the model part-downloaded. Send event → "The speech model has downloaded" to watch it become ready.
- "Typical": ready to use.

**Limits of the preview:** recording works there, but the fake server can't transcribe, so the box just comes back with what you'd typed.

I've added two proposed rules to `RULES.md`. The set-up and download are recorded in `NOTES.md`, with two open questions:
- **Changing or removing the model:** where should that live? Prelude has no settings page yet, so it could go on the project page or in a small menu on the microphone.
- **How Prelude runs Whisper:** the speech-to-text model can run through a Node library or a separate program. That's for the build to settle.

The page menu now lets you pick which record a page shows, and go to any URL. I haven't seen it render; Prelude's check after this turn will show whether it does. Press Reset data first, as the states changed again.

First, a correction to my original point 4: pages whose URL has a parameter (like `/offers/:id`) were already in the menu. Prelude fills them in with the state's first record. What's actually missing is choosing *which* record, so that's what I designed.

**The page menu**
- **Records under their page:** a page about one record lists, underneath it, every record the current state has for it. Each shows its label and a short note, such as "Harbor Lending · 7.05% · 48 months · expired". The long-name case and the expired offer are one click away, and the page shows how many records there are ("3 in this state").
- **The button says which record:** for example "Offer · Northwind Bank", cut short if long.
- **Overlays** (drawers, dialogs) are indented under their page, and open over the record you're looking at.
- **Go to a URL** sits at the end of the menu, for anything the list can't offer: a search with its query, or a record a form just added. A URL the design doesn't have leaves the page as it was and says so.
- **Refresh** and **Open in browser** come last, and act on the exact record.
- **Captures and the "looking at" chip** name the record too, so the agent knows which offer you mean.

**How records get their labels:** Prelude would use a field the route names, through a new `"label"` option in `routes.json`. Otherwise it uses the record's `name` or `title`, or else its id.

To try it, the "Doesn't render" state opens on the long-named credit union's offer.

**Design system:** menus can now have indented sub-rows, dividers between groups, and a small form with a real button at the end. Before, any button inside a menu was styled as a plain row.

**Questions for you:**
1. **The note under each record:** should `routes.json` name the fields it shows (`"note": ["rate", "term"]`), or is the label enough?
2. **Pages with hundreds of records:** should the menu show the first 20 and let you filter the rest as you type? The states here hold a handful, so I've left that for now.
